newsitem.title: ITALY: Govt ready to help Italy's weather-hit agriculture.
newsitem.headline: Govt ready to help Italy's weather-hit agriculture.

text.p: Italian Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto said on Thursday the government is ready to help out areas of the country where crops have been badly hit by abnormal weather conditions of severe drought and frost.
Pinto said in a statement his ministry was closely monitoring the situation in liaison with regional authorities to assess the amount of damage caused.
Areas hit would be given aid and loans out of a national fund which at the moment totalled 250 billion lire.
Officials from all Italy's 20 regions have been called to a meeting at the ministry on April 30 in order to quantify the damage to crops across the nation.
Pinto noted that while drought conditions in many parts of Italy had to some extent been eased by rainfall in recent days the alarm over frost was continuing.

Italy's national farmers' federation Coldiretti has said the unseasonal weather, with drought mainly in the north, rain in the south and frost throughout the country had caused crop damage of over two trillion lire.
Coldiretti called on the government to take urgent measures including declaring a state of emergency in at least three regions -- Piedmont, Lombardy and Veneto.
